metadata.title: Another proof of the analytic Hahn - Banach Theorem

nodes.name: Semi-norm
nodes.statement: A function $p : L \to [0,+\infty)$ is a \textit{semi-norm} if for every $x, y \in L$ and $\lambda \in \Phi$: $p(x+y) \leq p(x) + p(y)$ and $p(\lambda x) = |\lambda|\, p(x)$.
nodes.statement_clean: A non-negative function on a vector space that is subadditive and absolutely homogeneous.

nodes.name: Convex functional
nodes.statement: A function $\varphi : L \to \mathbb{R}$ is a \textit{convex functional} if for all $x, y \in L$ and $0 < \lambda < 1$: $\varphi(\lambda x + (1-\lambda)y) \leq \lambda \varphi(x) + (1-\lambda)\varphi(y)$.
nodes.statement_clean: A real-valued function on a vector space satisfying the standard convexity inequality.

nodes.name: Geometric Hahn-Banach Theorem (Separation)
nodes.statement: Let $L$ be a topological vector space, $M$ a linear manifold in $L$, and $G$ a non-empty convex open subset of $L$ not intersecting $M$. There exists a closed hyperplane in $L$ containing $M$ and not intersecting $G$.
nodes.statement_clean: A linear manifold disjoint from a non-empty convex open set can be separated from it by a closed hyperplane.
assumptions: $G \subset L$ is non-empty, convex, and open
conclusions: There exists a closed hyperplane $H_1 \subset L$ such that $M \subset H_1$ and $H_1 \cap G = \emptyset$
nodes.origin_citation: Schaeffer, Topological Vector Spaces, Theorem 3.1, p.46

nodes.name: Analytic Hahn-Banach Theorem (cited form)
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a subspace of a vector space $L$ over $\Phi$, and $p : L \to [0,+\infty)$ a semi-norm. If $g: M \to \Phi$ is linear with $|g(x)| \leq p(x)$ on $M$, then there exists a linear $f: L \to \Phi$ with $f|_M = g$ and $|f(x)| \leq p(x)$ on $L$.
nodes.statement_clean: Any linear functional on a subspace dominated by a semi-norm extends to a dominated linear functional on the whole space.
assumptions: $M$ is a subspace of a vector space $L$ over $\Phi$
conclusions: There exists a linear $f : L \to \Phi$ with $f|_M = g$
nodes.origin_citation: Schaeffer, Topological Vector Spaces, Theorem 3.2, p.47

nodes.name: Continuity equivalent to upper semi-continuity for convex functionals
nodes.statement: Let $L$ be a topological vector space over $\mathbb{R}$, $\mathfrak{B}$ the family of all circled $0$-neighborhoods, and $\varphi : L \to \mathbb{R}$ a convex functional. Then $\varphi$ is continuous on $L$ iff $\varphi$ is upper semi-continuous on $L$.
nodes.statement_clean: A convex functional on a real TVS is continuous iff it is upper semi-continuous.
assumptions: $L$ is a topological vector space over $\mathbb{R}$
conclusions: $\varphi$ is continuous on $L$ $\iff$ $\varphi$ is upper semi-continuous on $L$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma L_Dominated1.1
nodes.statement: One direction is immediate. For the converse, given $\varepsilon>0$ pick a circled $U_\varepsilon$ on which upper semi-continuity holds; combined with $2\varphi(x_0) \leq \varphi(x_0+u) + \varphi(x_0-u)$, conclude $|\varphi(x_0+u) - \varphi(x_0)| < \varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Forward direction is trivial
nodes.statement: If $\varphi$ is continuous on $L$, then $\varphi$ is upper semi-continuous on $L$ by definition of u.s.c.

nodes.name: Use upper semi-continuity at $x_0$
nodes.statement: Assume $\varphi$ is u.s.c. at $x_0$. Given $\varepsilon>0$, choose $U_\varepsilon \in \mathfrak{B}$ with $u \in U_\varepsilon \Rightarrow \max\{\varphi(x_0+u), \varphi(x_0-u)\} < \varphi(x_0) + \varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Apply convexity inequality
nodes.statement: By convexity, $2\varphi(x_0) \leq \varphi(x_0+u) + \varphi(x_0-u)$, hence $2\varphi(x_0) \leq \varphi(x_0+u) + \varphi(x_0-u) < 2\varphi(x_0) + 2\varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Combine bounds and conclude continuity
nodes.statement: Combining the upper bound with the convexity bound yields $\varphi(x_0) - \varepsilon < \varphi(x_0+u) < \varphi(x_0) + \varepsilon$ for $u \in U_\varepsilon$, so $\varphi$ is continuous at $x_0$.

nodes.name: Real Hahn-Banach extension via convex functional
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a subspace of a real vector space $L$, and $\varphi : L \to \mathbb{R}$ a convex functional with $\varphi(\lambda x) = \lambda \varphi(x)$ for $\lambda \geq 0$. If $g: M \to \mathbb{R}$ is linear with $g(x) \leq \varphi(x)$ on $M$, then there exists a linear $f: L \to \mathbb{R}$ extending $g$ with $f(x) \leq \varphi(x)$ on $L$.
nodes.statement_clean: Real-valued linear functionals dominated by a positively homogeneous convex functional extend to the whole space.
assumptions: $M$ is a subspace of a vector space $L$ over $\mathbb{R}$
conclusions: There exists a linear $f : L \to \mathbb{R}$ with $f|_M = g$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma L_Dominated1.2
nodes.statement: Equip $L$ with the topology generated by $V_n = U_n \cap (-U_n)$, $U_n = \{\varphi < 1/n\}$; show $\varphi$ is continuous. Apply the geometric Hahn-Banach (Theorem T_Separation) to separate $H = \{g(x)-t=1\}$ from the open convex $G = \{\varphi(x)-t<1\}$ in $L\times\mathbb{R}$. Recover $f$ from the separating functional.

nodes.name: Construct $0$-neighborhood base $\mathfrak{B}$
nodes.statement: Define $U_n = \{x \in L : \varphi(x) < 1/n\}$ and $\mathfrak{B} = \{V_n = U_n \cap (-U_n) : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$. Verify (a) $V_{2n}+V_{2n} \subset V_n$ and (b) each $V_n$ is radial and circled.

nodes.name: Endow $L$ with TVS topology $\mathfrak{T}$
nodes.statement: By Corollary of Statement 2.1 in Schaeffer (p.15), $\mathfrak{B}$ is a $0$-neighborhood base for a unique topology $\mathfrak{T}$ making $L$ a topological vector space.

nodes.name: Show $\varphi$ is upper semi-continuous, hence continuous
nodes.statement: For arbitrary $w_0 \in L$ and $\varepsilon>0$, pick $n_\varepsilon$ with $u \in V_{n_\varepsilon} \Rightarrow \varphi(w_0+u) \leq \varphi(w_0) + \varphi(u) < \varphi(w_0) + \varepsilon$. Thus $\varphi$ is u.s.c. on $L$, and by Lemma L_Dominated1.1, $\varphi$ is continuous.

nodes.name: Define hyperplane $H$ and open convex set $G$
nodes.statement: Set $H = \{(x,t) \in M \times \mathbb{R} : g(x) - t = 1\}$, a hyperplane in $M \times \mathbb{R}$ and linear manifold in $L \times \mathbb{R}$; and $G = \{(x,t) \in L \times \mathbb{R} : \varphi(x) - t < 1\}$, an open non-empty convex set with $G \cap H = \emptyset$ since $g \leq \varphi$ on $M$.

nodes.name: Apply geometric Hahn-Banach (Theorem T_Separation)
nodes.statement: By Theorem \ref{T_Separation}, there exists a hyperplane $H_1 \subset L \times \mathbb{R}$ with $H_1 \supset H$ and $H_1 \cap G = \emptyset$.

nodes.name: Show $H_1 \cap (M \times \mathbb{R}) = H$
nodes.statement: Pick $(x_0, t_0) \in H_1 \cap (M \times \mathbb{R})$. Since $(0,0) \notin H_1$ but $(0,0) \in M \times \mathbb{R}$, $H_1 \cap (M \times \mathbb{R})$ is a proper hyperplane in $M \times \mathbb{R}$ containing $H$, hence equals $H$.

nodes.name: Represent $H_1$ via a linear functional $F$
nodes.statement: By Statement 4.1 in Schaeffer (p.24), $H_1 = \{(x,t) : F(x,t) = 1\}$ for some non-zero linear $F : L \times \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$. Setting $f(\cdot) := F(\cdot, 0)$ gives $f|_M = g$, and $(0,-1) \in H$ forces $F(x,t) = f(x) - t$.

nodes.name: Verify $f \leq \varphi$ on $L$
nodes.statement: On $H_1$: $f(x) = 1 + t \leq \varphi(x)$. For $(x,t) \notin H_1$, choose $r \neq 1$ with $f(x) - t = r$; then $(x, t+r-1) \in H_1$, yielding $f(x) \leq \varphi(x)$.

nodes.name: Analytic Hahn-Banach Theorem (main result, complex case)
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a subspace of a complex vector space $L$ and $p : L \to [0,+\infty)$ a semi-norm. If $g : M \to \mathbb{C}$ is linear with $|g(x)| \leq p(x)$ on $M$, then there exists a linear $f : L \to \mathbb{C}$ with $f|_M = g$ and $|f(x)| \leq p(x)$ on $L$.
nodes.statement_clean: Hahn-Banach extension theorem for complex linear functionals dominated by a semi-norm.
assumptions: $M$ is a subspace of a vector space $L$ over $\mathbb{C}$
conclusions: There exists a linear $f : L \to \mathbb{C}$ with $f|_M = g$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem T_Dominated1
nodes.statement: Decompose $g(x) = g_0(x) - i g_0(ix)$ for some real-linear $g_0$. Apply Lemma L_Dominated1.2 to $g_0$ and $p$ to obtain real-linear $f_0$ with $f_0|_M = g_0$ and $f_0 \leq p$. Define $f(x) = f_0(x) - i f_0(ix)$; verify extension and use $f(x) = |f(x)| e^{i\theta(x)}$ to bound $|f|$ by $p$.

nodes.name: Decompose complex linear functional into real part
nodes.statement: There exists a real-linear $g_0 : M \to \mathbb{R}$ with $g(x) = g_0(x) - i g_0(ix)$ for all $x \in M$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma L_Dominated1.2 to obtain $f_0$
nodes.statement: Since $p$ is a convex functional with $p(\lambda x) = \lambda p(x)$ for $\lambda \geq 0$, regarding $L$ as a real linear space and applying Lemma L_Dominated1.2 yields real-linear $f_0 : L \to \mathbb{R}$ with $f_0|_M = g_0$ and $f_0(x) \leq p(x)$ on $L$.

nodes.name: Define complex extension $f$
nodes.statement: Define $f : L \to \mathbb{C}$ by $f(x) = f_0(x) - i f_0(ix)$. Then $f$ is $\mathbb{C}$-linear; for $x \in M$, $f(x) = g_0(x) - i g_0(ix) = g(x)$, so $f$ extends $g$.

nodes.name: Bound $|f(x)|$ via polar argument
nodes.statement: Writing $f(x) = |f(x)| e^{i\theta(x)}$, we have $|f(x)| = f_0(x / e^{i\theta(x)}) \leq p(x/e^{i\theta(x)}) = p(x)$, completing the proof.

nodes.name: Upper-semicontinuity inequality
nodes.statement: $u \in U_\varepsilon \Rightarrow \max\{\varphi(x_0 + u), \varphi(x_0 - u)\} < \varphi(x_0) + \varepsilon$

nodes.name: Convexity inequality at $x_0 \pm u$
nodes.statement: $2\varphi(x_0) \leq \varphi(x_0 + u) + \varphi(x_0 - u)$

nodes.name: Hyperplane bound on $H_1$
nodes.statement: $f(x) = 1 + t \leq \varphi(x)$ for all $(x,t) \in H_1$.
